deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an administrative receipt (Quittung) written in Göttingen on 21 January 1858 and signed 'B. Riemann, Professor'. In it Riemann confirms that he received his salary for the winter semester from Michaelis 1857 to Easter 1858 from the Royal University Treasury (Königliche Universitäts-Casse) in Hanover. The payment came from his annual remuneration of 200 Thaler Courant, which was raised to 300 Thaler from 1 November 1857. The amount received is 141 Thaler 16 gute Groschen Courant.

The only computation behind the page is how this amount was arrived at. The following reconstruction is mine; the page states only the result.
- Treat the semester as six months, October through March. Michaelis is 29 September; Easter 1858 fell on 4 April.
- One month (October 1857) at the old rate: 200/12 = 16 2/3 Thaler.
- Five months (November 1857 to March 1858) at the new rate: 5 × 300/12 = 125 Thaler.
- Total: 141 2/3 Thaler.
- In Hanoverian Courant, 1 Thaler = 24 gute Groschen, so 2/3 Thaler = 16 Ggr.
- The total is therefore 141 Thaler 16 Ggr, exactly the sum written on the page in both figures and words.

The written-out amount shows a correction in the hundreds/units word. It now reads 'Einhundert ein und vierzig', with the struck word apparently 'zwei'. This agrees with the figure 141.

Historical context: Riemann was a Privatdozent with a 200-Thaler remuneration (granted c. 1855–56). He was named außerordentlicher Professor in November 1857, and this receipt records the matching pay rise to 300 Thaler from 1 November 1857.

results.what: Pro-rata salary calculation: 1 month at 200 Thlr/yr plus 5 months at 300 Thlr/yr = 141 Thlr 16 Ggr. This is a biographical/administrative record of Riemann's salary increase on becoming extraordinary professor (Nov. 1857).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine salary receipt with no mathematical content. The facts it records are well known from Riemann biographies (Dedekind's memoir; Laugwitz): his 200-Thaler remuneration and its increase to 300 Thaler on his promotion to extraordinary professor in November 1857.

transcription_corrections: The amount in words reads 'Einhundert ein und vierzig Thaler sechzehn Ggr. Ct.'. The struck word is probably 'zwei', corrected to 'ein', consistent with the figure 141.
'Logenmeister' is doubtful. The paying official is more plausibly a 'Cassenmeister' or similar treasury officer; the name read as 'Heimann' is also uncertain.
The header abbreviation 'rthl' is rendered in the original with the Thaler symbol (a ß-like sign), as is '300 rthl'.
